children: Enterprise technology major International Business Machines Corp. (IBM, Financials) had better-than-expected third quarter profits but faced market doubts about the sustainability of its software recovery.

Revenue rose 4.7 percent to $17.10 billion, surpassing the Wall Street forecast of $16.82 billion. Adjusted profit of $2.95 a share also bested estimates of $2.86. Software was the standout item of the quarter.
Revenue from the division was up to $7.80 billion and IBM raised its annual software growth outlook to around 7% to 8% from 6% to 8%.
But the improvement came with a caveat.

Some of the software contracts that concluded during the quarter were deferred from the prior period. That generated issues about whether faster increase reflects new demand or just business moving from one quarter to the next.
Software revenue rose greater than 8% and hybrid cloud sales were up 11%.
But IBM must now show investors it can keep the rally alive as the advantage of those deferred contracts fades.
The next catalyst will be whether fourth quarter software bookings are high enough to match the increased growth expectation.

title: IBM's Software Rebound Comes With a Catch
